judgments.identity: Entrypoint SDK Linux x64 platform bundle, with Entrypoint connector and official FRP client 0.71.1
evidence: Manifest ships only two binaries and has no lifecycle hooks or dependencies.
Parent SDK 0.2.0 calls spawn only from explicitly invoked tunnel(); it requires a supplied connection bundle and upstream address.
Connector main at 0xd378e0 dispatches tunnel, vpn, rebundle and version. It fails without connection bundles; no baked-in attacker connection bundle was found.
Tunnel decoding parses epc1 Base64url JSON, validates the gateway port, CA list and token; server and upstream values come from caller configuration.
Connector.Run at 0xd31780 creates a temporary directory, restricts permissions to 0700, writes CA/configuration with 0600, starts frpc and removes its own temporary directory on exit.
runFrpc at 0xd338e0 launches the configured executable with the argument vector [-c, configPath]; the token is passed via environment. Parent stdin accepts only drain/drained/stop lifecycle commands.

RunVPN at 0xd35220 requires caller-selected expose/forward endpoints and a supplied epv1 bundle. It joins a configured Headscale/Tailscale control URL, then relays TCP traffic using paired io.Copy calls. VPN identity state is saved in the user configuration directory.
TLS is verified using bundle CAs by default; certificate-verification bypass is an explicit development option.

Credential-like/private-key strings are PKI, Tailscale and token-handling support, not evidence of credential harvesting. Decoded constant strings include certificate fragments and incidental decoder candidates, not an executed hidden script.
The FRP member SHA-256 35c6054d4549bbcf2f02875543895fd9e44c2aae2925f61cd8ff5a693703c28b is identical to the official 0.71.1 release binary.

Rebuilding connector source at its embedded VCS revision with Go 1.27.2 reproduces the complete .gopclntab. Comparing all x86-64 .text instructions found no differences except address displacements caused by build metadata layout; printable .rodata differences are VCS metadata and one incidental address-shaped run.
judgments.provenance_disagreement: GHSA and the OSV record give generic compromise advice without an explained malicious code path; OSV imports the same GHSA and is not independent behavioral evidence. OSM returned a JavaScript page without accessible case details. A dual-use tunnel/FRP classification is a plausible cause of the external label, but its actual origin cannot be established.
judgments.missing_context: No deployed connection bundle, gateway ownership or authorization context was supplied. Unauthorized use would change the deployment judgment.
